modelResponse.episodeSummary: Richard M. Calloway, Ventricular Tachycardia, critical, hemodynamically stable
keyECGEvidence: morphology: Wide monomorphic QRS, RBBB-like morphology with monophasic R in V1 (not typical rSR'), left axis deviation, QS pattern in V6; AV dissociation with 2 capture beats visible; precordial concordance (negative) in V1-V4
preEventNote: Baseline ECG: sinus rhythm with old anterior Q waves, LVEF 35% on recent echo
contributingFactors: Prior anterior MI (2020, PCI to LAD)

rejectedAlternatives.why: QRS duration 156ms is wide, morphology is monomorphic with AV dissociation (capture beats visible) and negative concordance, strongly suggesting VT, not SVT with aberrancy.
Rate is too fast (165 bpm) and rhythm is regular, inconsistent with AIVR.
Potassium 4.2 mmol/L and Magnesium 2.0 mg/dL are within normal limits.
Patient is not on digoxin. No other drug toxicity suggested by data.

recommendedActions: Administer Amiodarone 300 mg IV push over 10 minutes (check for contraindications)
Consider Lidocaine 1-1.5 mg/kg IV push if Amiodarone is contraindicated or ineffective
Prepare for cardioversion if hemodynamics deteriorate or VT persists after pharmacologic therapy
Evaluate for underlying ischemia (e.g., repeat ECG after termination, consider coronary angiography)
Hold Carvedilol until rhythm is stable and hemodynamics assessed
uncertainty: Exact location and extent of scar tissue contributing to VT is unknown.
Presence of ongoing ischemia contributing to VT cannot be fully excluded without further investigation.
